evidenceDecision: Real notification listener/push tests and durable task notification tests exercise session-safe clicks, endpoint validation and persist-before-dispatch/dedup across restart. Owner asks (#472): direct store and browser cases check one announcement per retained ask ID, initial-backlog suppression, revision/socket retirement, local OS delivery with Web Push selected and exact original-terminal/session notification admission. #493: store cases name the asker (Herdr's agent name, an unverified mark once) with the question's first line, announce an unverified ask only when the service placed it on one local pane, and never announce a dismissed ask; the asks store sends the owner's dismissal through world.ask.dismiss. These tests do not claim delivery while every browser is closed. SQLite attention supplements this assessment under openspec/specs/world-storage/spec.md: finite source/compiled crash schedules prove acknowledged-answer retention, atomic outbox commits, one writer, import/reopen and explicit effect-class uncertainty. Owner alerts may repeat; uncertain pane answers never auto-replay. Synthetic receiver deduplication is not attributed to Herdr. Question closure (#1128) selects an exhaustive alternative to a new Quint model: 256 identity cases and 120 serial orders in world-question-ownership.test.ts, real SQLite race/reopen/RPC and production DOM controls; downstream lease and answer-recipient models remain unchanged. Supplemental finite source/compiled recovery, root fail-stop, base32 allocation and Reception evidence require independent review under the World storage contract; accepted model claims are unchanged. Questions across World instances (#1152) reuse the home's single serialized ledger as the only authority, so no new interleaving needs a model: real two-World service tests on one synthetic runtime race answers from both Worlds and record exactly one, forward dismissals, drop a stopped home's questions and keep a question on the runtime captured at ask time after its saved connection is retargeted; unit cases check alert routing within Herdr's 400-character body through the production decoder, every accepted World name, peer-route refusals and bounded alert-only entries. Issue #1437 adds a finite foreground admission matrix in server/src/adapters/agent-input.test.ts and server/src/world/answer-foreground.test.ts: both native input methods, refused foreground classes, original-session replacement around preparation, and both runtimes at answer/dispatch/final-input boundaries retain zero input, Reception refusal, ask get and no revival. Native-send tests cover observed held-send cancellation. Existing lease/effect models own unchanged generation and uncertain-recovery ordering; this monotone admission predicate needs no additional state model. The full gate remains required; no atomic OS foreground compare-and-send or live-runtime guarantee is claimed. Owner repair covers shell/editor children in the existing World+storage integration matrix, unavailable foreground reads remaining pending, and node-launched ask capture. Outbox browser and qualified composer request checks cover explicit copy/draft-only recovery without an effect send; restart/upgrade remain non-reattaching and retrievable. No new delivery state or automatic replay is added.
